title: Forming Giant-sized Polymersomes Using Gel-assisted Rehydration
protocol: Prepare a 5 mg/ml solution of polymer in chloroform.
Add 1 ml of chloroform to 5 mg of solid poly(ethylene oxide)-b-poly(butadiene) (PEO-PBD, EO22-BD37) diblock copolymer in a glass vial.
Swirl the vial to fully dissolve the polymer.
Mix a fluorescently labeled lipid at a 0.5 mol % final concentration with 99.5 mol % unlabeled polymer.
Pipette ~12 μl of a 1 mg/ml fluorescently labeled lipid in chloroform into 997.58 μl PEO-PBD, EO22-BD37 polymer in chloroform.
Store the solution in an airtight vial with a chloroform-resistant lid at -20 °C.
Wrap plumbers tape on vial edge where the lid screws onto the vial and secure the lid on the vial.
Wrap another piece of plumbers tape on the outside of the lid.
Finally, wrap Parafilm on the outside of the tape to ensure minimal evaporation.
Mix 0.5 mg of standard agarose in 50 ml water (or 50 ml 100 mM sucrose) in a 250 ml Erlenmeyer flask.
Boil the agarose solution in a microwave for ~1 min (or until fully dissolved).
Cut the end off of a 1,000 µl pipette tip to prevent clogging.
Pipette 300 µl of melted agarose solution onto a 25 mm square glass coverslip using the cut pipette tip.
Allow the agarose to cool to ~65-75 °C prior to spreading.
Hold just the edge of the coverslip with gloved fingers and use the long edge of another 1,000 µl pipette tip to spread the agarose evenly across the surface.
Move the pipette tip back and forth until the agarose completely adheres to and covers the coverslip.
Place the agarose-coated coverslip onto a piece of Parafilm with the agarose facing up.
Place the Parafilm with the coverslips into a 37 °C incubator for at least 1 hr.
Pipette 30 μl prepared polymer solution onto the agarose film.
Spread the polymer solution across the agarose films using a circular motion until evaporated, holding just the edge of the coverslip with gloved fingers and using an 18 G needle.
Place the polymer films in a plastic Petri dish polymer side facing up.
Put the Petri dish into a standard house vacuum desiccator covered in aluminum foil for at least 1 hr to remove residual solvent.
Adhere a coverwell, either home-made PDMS well or commercially available well, to the coverslip coated with the polymer film.
Press the coverwell gently onto the polymer-coated coverslip until a tight seal is formed.
Add 200-500 µl rehydration solution to the chamber.
Place a rolled, wet Kimwipe along the edges of a glass Petri dish.
Place the polymer film with the adhered coverwell into the humidity chamber and cover with a lid.
Cover the Petri dish with aluminum foil.
Place the Petri dish onto a hot plate set to 40 °C for at least 30 min.
Use a 100X oil objective to focus on the top surface of the coverslip where the polymersomes will be adhered.
Identify the polymersomes using fluorescence microscopy.
Characterize membrane fluidity using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) on a fluorescence microscope containing an adjustable condenser.
Focus the microscope on the polymersome of interest.
Close the condenser to a small region and ensure that the edge of a polymersome is within the imaging region of interest.
Increase the camera exposure and ensure all neutral density filters are removed to effectively photobleach the region of interest.
Allow the membrane fluorescence intensity to photobleach for 7-10 seconds or until the fluorescence intensity is significantly decreased.
Turn off the lamp and fully open the condenser.
Decrease the exposure back to the starting settings.
Begin immediately capturing images every 30 seconds for 3 minutes.
Calculate membrane diffusion coefficients using standard methods.
If the bleached region regains fluorescence intensity within 3-5 minutes, indicate that the membrane is fluid.
Open acquired images of polymersomes in image analysis software.
Set the scale for the image by clicking on the analyze drop-down box and then "set scale".
Calibrate the scale for the microscope using standard methods (i.e., a micrometer).
Fill in the calibration units and click "ok".
Click on the line tool box and draw a line spanning the diameter of a vesicle.
Collect length measurements by clicking on the analyze drop-down box and clicking "measure".
Continue measuring individual vesicles following the above procedure.
Press "Ctrl + D" after drawing each line and measuring the length to imprint the line drawn onto the image.
